notes:
Last night before the memo, so I'm closing out the three loose threads that actually change what I tell Marco and Tobias, and skipping anything merely confirmatory:

1. The orphan subscription-delivery report came back strange: 0% of orphan customers were classified as "lapsed within 30 days" and 0% as "no subscription record at all" — yet 25-46% of orders are orphan. That means essentially all orphan customers have a subscription record, just not one whose status/date my query treated as active-and-overlapping. The likely candidates are 'paused' or 'incomplete' subscriptions, or cancellations that happened well before the 30-day window I checked. I need the actual status distribution before I can tell Tobias whether this is "paused customers still getting free boxes" (a real control gap) or something more benign.

2. The corrected (pre-discount subtotal) lift report is strikingly consistent — every one of the 50 worst rows shows negative lift, and the pattern looks structural, not noise. But it's fragmented into 219 rows at the per-tenant-instance grain, which is too granular for the memo's headline number. I want one clean, order-weighted summary per promotion family (Welcome10 / Black Friday / January Sale / Summer Sale) so Marco and Tobias get a single defensible "no incremental lift, if anything smaller baskets" figure rather than a page of tenant fragments.

3. The returns/refunds report surfaced two outsized ratios — a Welcome10 instance refunding 189% of its own discount cost, and a Volume-tier-10+ instance refunding 162% of its discount cost. Before stating "this discount is actively loss-making after refunds" in the memo, I want to check whether that's driven by a handful of large refunds (an outlier/concentration story, possibly one big account) versus broad-based returns across many orders (a genuine pattern worth capping the discount over).

These three reports close out Marco's Q3/Q4 and Tobias's Q1/Q2 with concrete, checked numbers for Friday.

requests.title: Subscription status distribution behind orphan comped-delivery orders
requests.question: What subscription status do the 'orphan' Subscription-delivery-discount customers (no active subscription overlap found) actually have on record, since neither 'lapsed within 30 days' nor 'no subscription at all' explained them?
requests.grain: one row per subscription-status category (trialing, active, past_due, canceled, paused, incomplete, or 'no_subscription_record')
columns: status category (customer's most recent subscription status for that tenant, by started_at, or 'no_subscription_record' if none exists)
orphan customer count
orphan order count (2025 'Subscription delivery (prepaid)' orders with no active-status date overlap, as defined in the prior report)
% of all orphan orders
avg days between subscription's ended_at (or current date if still open) and the orphan order's placed_at, where applicable
total discount amount on these orders (EUR)
requests.details: Source: same orphan-order population as the prior report (order_discounts + discounts name='Subscription delivery (prepaid)' + orders placed_at in 2025, status != 'cancelled', with no overlapping subscription of status in ('trialing','active','past_due') per the prior definition). For each orphan order's customer (user_id, tenant_id), find their single most recent subscription record by started_at and report its status (not restricted to active ones this time) as the category, or 'no_subscription_record' if the customer has zero subscription rows for that tenant. Convert discount amounts to EUR via exchange_rates (base_code='EUR', quote_code=currency_code, as_of=placed_at). Order by orphan order count descending. Print all categories (expect 5-8 rows).
builds_on: Subscription-delivery discount orders with no overlapping active subscription

requests.title: Aggregate within-customer basket-size lift by promotion family, 2025
requests.question: Across all tenants running each major marketing promotion, do customers buy bigger baskets (pre-discount subtotal) when using the code, stated as one clean weighted number per promotion family?
requests.grain: one row per promotion family name: 'Welcome 10% off', 'Black Friday 2025', 'January Sale 2025', 'Summer Sale 2025'
columns: promotion name
discount instances aggregated (distinct discounts.id count across tenants)
discounted order count (sum across all instances)
distinct customers (sum across instances, not deduplicated across tenants)
avg discounted order subtotal, order-weighted (EUR)
avg comparison order subtotal (same customers' other non-discounted 2025 orders), order-weighted (EUR)
subtotal lift (EUR)
subtotal lift (%)
% of discounted customers who had at least one comparison order
requests.details: Source: order_discounts + discounts (name in the four promotion names above, across all tenants/instances) + orders (subtotal, currency_code, placed_at in 2025, status != 'cancelled', user_id, tenant_id). For each promotion name, sum subtotal_eur and count across all discounted orders tenant-wide to get the order-weighted average (i.e. total EUR / total orders, not an average of per-tenant averages). For comparison, for every (user_id, tenant_id) that appears as a discounted customer under that promotion name, pull all their other 2025 orders for that tenant with no row in order_discounts, and similarly sum subtotal_eur and count across all of them tenant-wide for the order-weighted comparison average. Convert to EUR via exchange_rates (base_code='EUR', quote_code=currency_code, as_of=placed_at). Order by subtotal lift (%) ascending. Print all 4 rows.
builds_on: Corrected incrementality read: pre-discount basket size on top marketing discounts, 2025

requests.title: Concentration of refund cost on the two highest refund-to-discount-ratio instances
requests.question: For the two discount instances whose total refunds exceeded their own discount cost (Welcome 10% off with 260 orders, Volume tier 10+ with 104 orders, both from the prior return-rate report), is that refund cost driven by a handful of large refunds or spread broadly across many orders?
requests.grain: one row per discount instance (2 rows)
columns: discount name
order count (used to confirm identity: 260 for Welcome 10% off, 104 for Volume tier 10+)
total refunded amount, status='refunded' (EUR)
refund count (number of refunded order_returns)
top 3 single refunds as % of total refunded amount
median single refund amount (EUR)
max single refund amount (EUR)
% of this discount's orders that were refunded in full (refund_total >= order grand_total)
requests.details: Source: identify the two discount_id instances exactly as in the prior return-rate report — discounts.name='Welcome 10% off' whose set of 2025 non-cancelled orders (via order_discounts) numbers exactly 260, and discounts.name='Volume tier 10+' whose matching order set numbers exactly 104. For those two discount_ids, pull order_returns (status='refunded') joined to orders (grand_total, currency_code) for the orders carrying that discount, convert refund_total to EUR via exchange_rates (base_code='EUR', quote_code=currency_code, as_of=refunded_at date). Compute total, count, median, max, top-3-as-%-of-total, and % of orders fully refunded. Order by discount name ascending. Print both rows.
builds_on: Return and refund rates on discounted orders vs. baseline, 2025
